title: A boundary integral method for wave scattering in a heterogeneous medium with a moving obstacle
summary: We propose a time-domain boundary integral method to model linear wave propagation with refractive, focusing, and Doppler effects arising from medium heterogeneities and moving obstacles. In contrast to existing techniques, our method avoids volumetric discretization and yields a formulation posed only on the boundary of the obstacle. We combine two classical ingredients: a geometric--optics parametrix to capture leading-order behavior at propagating wavefronts, and a ray-based characterization of the distorted causal geometry.
